items.title: "FIGHT" button text confuses countdown with round number
items.what: In the pre-fight screens (e.g., screenshots #2, #10, #13), the large gold button reads "FIGHT 2", "FIGHT 3", and "FIGHT 4". Since the top-left HUD displays "ROUND 1/5", a player will likely interpret "FIGHT 4" as "Fight Number 4" or "Round 4" rather than a 4-second countdown timer.
items.why: This creates confusion about the game state. Players might hesitate, thinking the button indicates progression to a later stage rather than an imminent start, breaking the flow of the bout.
items.how: Change the button text to dynamically display "STARTING... 4", "3", "2", "1", and finally "FIGHT!" in large text, removing the static "FIGHT" label during the countdown phase.

items.title: Score fraction "2 1/2" is hard to parse quickly
items.what: In the Game Over screen (screenshot #8), the final score is displayed as "0 — 2½". The fraction character is visually dense and smaller than the integers, making it harder to read at a glance compared to the rest of the HUD.
items.why: In a competitive game, score clarity is paramount. Fractions require more cognitive load to parse than decimals, and the mixed formatting (integer vs fraction) looks inconsistent.
items.how: Switch the score display to use decimals (e.g., "2.5") which are standard in digital interfaces and instantly recognizable.

items.title: Fighters are too small in landscape orientation
items.what: In the landscape screenshot (#9), the fighters occupy less than 20% of the screen height, appearing tiny and distant. The dojo background dominates the frame, and the fighters' details (stances, spacing) are lost.
items.why: For a fighting game, seeing the spacing and animation of the fighters is critical. In landscape mode, the action is illegible, making the game feel broken or unpolished on wider screens.
items.how: Implement a responsive camera adjustment that zooms in (increases fighter scale) when the aspect ratio is landscape, cropping the background if necessary to keep the fighters prominent.

items.title: Ugly browser focus outline on Settings toggle
items.what: In the High Contrast settings screenshot (#15), the "Left-handed layout" row has a thick, white rectangular border around it. This is a default browser focus ring that has not been styled or removed.
items.why: It looks like a bug or unstyled HTML element, breaking the immersion and the "cinematic" art direction. It signals a lack of polish in the web implementation.
items.how: Add CSS `outline: none;` to the interactive elements or style the `:focus` state to match the game's UI (e.g., a subtle gold glow) to maintain the aesthetic.

items.title: Move name feedback is too subtle compared to score events
items.what: When a move is executed (e.g., "LUNGE PUNCH" in #5, "FRONT KICK" in #12), the text appears in a small, dark pill with white text. This is visually weak compared to the massive, glowing gold "IPPON" text in screenshot #11.
items.why: Players need immediate, clear confirmation that their input registered, especially during the "wind-up" phase mentioned in the tips. The current feedback is easy to miss and feels like a debug label.
items.how: Increase the font size of the move name, change the text color to the HUD gold/yellow, and remove the dark background pill so the text floats more prominently over the action, similar to the "QUALIFIER" text style.
